title: The house
lead: Nothing here exists until you ask for it.
story: Gwadlas is a bespoke house in Pretoria. We don’t keep stock and we don’t make collections: every piece starts on a blank page, with a conversation about who it is for and where it will be worn.

We work mostly in South African cloth: indigo and brown shweshwe, umbhaco cotton with black braid, and glass beadwork from the Eastern Cape. We also draw on cloth and technique from across the continent: adire, kente, agbada embroidery and raffia.
Each garment is drafted from your measurements, fitted on you two to four times, and cut, sewn and beaded by hand in South Africa.

quote.text: My grandmother’s umbhaco skirt was the starting point. They kept her braid pattern and cut it into something I can wear to work.
